label: Household financial resources
definition: Income and material resources available to priority-group households before housing and energy costs. Distinct from neighborhood-average wealth.

label: Resident decision-making influence
definition: Neighborhood-level effective collective influence over planning, budgets and housing decisions. Influence can favor affluent newcomers; a neighborhood gain is not automatically greater voice for original priority residents.

label: Local public investment
definition: Realized public spending on the focal neighborhood's housing, infrastructure and services. Its equity effect depends on allocation and resident retention.

label: Equity policy response
definition: Implemented response to monitored inequities, including resourcing and enforcement. An explicitly conditional institutional response, not an automatic reaction.

label: Affordable housing protection
definition: Effective provision and preservation of affordable secure homes, tenant protections and anti-displacement measures for priority residents.

label: Neighborhood socioeconomic resources
definition: Average resources of the resident population; changes may reflect who can afford to enter or remain. A compositional variable, not incumbent household income.

label: Healthy housing quality
definition: Priority residents' access to homes with adequate ventilation, moisture control, thermal comfort and safe materials; energy performance is separately represented.

label: Housing energy efficiency
definition: Energy performance of priority households' homes, with adequate ventilation and comfort maintained; implementation costs are not assumed away.

label: Energy cost burden
definition: Required household energy expenditure relative to resources, excluding rent or mortgage payments; higher means greater financial strain.

label: Housing cost burden
definition: Rent or mortgage and mandatory tenure costs relative to priority household resources; excludes the separately modeled household energy burden.

label: Local housing costs
definition: Local rents and purchase prices faced by entrants and renewing residents; price increases do not imply existing residents become wealthier.

label: Gentrification pressure
definition: Market-led neighborhood upgrading and socioeconomic replacement pressure. Effects depend on tenure, timing, safeguards and local institutions.

label: Housing insecurity
definition: Priority residents' uncertainty about retaining an adequate, affordable home; includes threatened loss and unstable tenure.

label: Involuntary displacement
definition: Forced or financially compelled residential moves among original priority residents; distinct from all residential mobility or cultural change alone.

label: Walkable land-use mix
definition: Connected proximity of everyday destinations and complementary uses. Density alone is deliberately not treated as uniformly beneficial.

label: Inclusive public transport access
definition: Affordable, physically accessible, reliable public transport that meets priority groups' destinations and travel needs; distance to a stop alone is insufficient.

label: Safe walking and cycling infrastructure
definition: Usable routes, safe crossings, separation and speed management, adapted to age, disability and other access needs.

label: Active travel and physical activity
definition: Walking, cycling and other physical activity among priority residents; benefits depend on access, safety and exposure conditions.

label: Car-dependent travel
definition: Reliance on private motorized travel for everyday needs; changing this requires viable alternatives rather than simply restricting mobility.

label: Motor traffic volume
definition: Motor-vehicle traffic in places used by priority residents, with background fleet, road design and speeds held in context.

label: Green and public-space quality
definition: Maintained, welcoming and effectively accessible shared green/public spaces for priority residents, rather than green acreage alone.

label: Effective local service access
definition: Ability to use affordable, appropriate local services, including healthcare, healthy food and community amenities; includes financial and physical accessibility.

label: Social cohesion
definition: Inclusive trust, support and collective capacity among original priority residents; exclusionary bonding is not counted as an equity benefit.

label: Neighborhood disorder
definition: Neglect and environmental disorder of shared places, without treating poverty or demographic composition itself as disorder.

label: Perceived neighborhood safety
definition: Priority residents' perceived safety from crime and traffic danger when using streets and shared places; perceptions may differ from measured risk.

label: Traffic injury risk
definition: Population-level injury risk to priority residents from road traffic; not risk per walking trip. More exposure can raise injuries in unsafe conditions.

label: Air pollution exposure
definition: Priority residents' exposure to harmful outdoor pollutants. Traffic emissions are one driver; local dispersion and other sources remain contextual.

label: Noise exposure
definition: Harmful environmental noise affecting priority residents; unequal exposure is context-dependent rather than assumed in every city.

label: Heat exposure
definition: Harmful heat experienced by priority residents, conditional on shade, dwelling conditions, cooling access and individual vulnerability.

label: Chronic stress
definition: Persistent psychosocial stress associated with financial strain, insecurity, environmental conditions and constrained control.

label: Physical ill health
definition: Physical morbidity and functional limitations in priority residents. The model represents direction, not a fitted disease incidence rate.

label: Mental ill health
definition: Adverse mental health among priority residents, distinguished from stress as a mediating experience; no diagnosis is inferred for individuals.

label: Work participation
definition: Priority residents' ability to obtain and sustain paid work. The health-to-work link is a synthesis hypothesis sensitive to labor protections.

label: Unmet-needs disparity
definition: Excess unmet built-environment needs among priority groups relative to a locally defined, better-served reference group. Higher means less equity. A conceptual set of domain-specific gaps, with no invented weighting or scalar score.

label: Health inequity
definition: Unfair, avoidable excess physical and mental ill health among priority groups relative to the local reference group; health inequality requires normative assessment to call it inequity.
